about: PlanCost across plan variants (literal, no-sieve, tuned) against the measured spills and, where a clean same-session clock phase exists, wall-clock, per (cell, card) (felizjueves.performance.planrank, #165). Does a plan with fewer counted intermediates spill less; does one with fewer FLOPs run faster? Reads both sides, feeds neither: nothing here reaches PlanCost or a literature floor. An order, never a prediction. Recomputed by test/test_planrank.py.

header.plan: plan.pipeline.plan(spec).cost: flops summed over batches, max_intermediates maxed over batches, of the plan the kernel is built from (sieved unless no-sieve; the recorded search if tuned).
header.spill: max_intermediates against the row's spill_store + spill_load, over every two variants of a cell with a compiled row. sm_86: bytes; gfx1200: spilled register counts. Within a card only.
header.clock: flops against lever_ab's same-session sign (#60's rule), for (literal, arm) only: a no-sieve row and a tuned row were timed in different sessions, so that pair is never formed. Per input, judged apart.
header.clean: an arm row timed against its same-session control, its four gate readings on that input known and <= 30% (gate.GPU_BUSY_MAX). Anything else is listed as not clean with its reason, never imputed.
header.classes: no_claim: the measurement ties. noise_floor: same text (source_sha256), measured apart. unresolved: the plan ties. concordant: the plan's cheaper variant measures better. discordant: it measures worse -- an inversion, named in summary.
header.verdict: per card and claim: predicts iff concordant > 0 and discordant = 0; inverts iff the reverse; mixed iff both; not shown iff neither. The counts predict the kernel on a card iff every claim there predicts. Written after #162's and #163's rows were read: a reading, never a choice (#166 decides the default).
header.spearman: kernelrank.spearman: per cell over its variants (spill), and per card over the pairs' relative changes. A handful of points: an order, never a prediction interval or a pooled score.

sm_86.answer: On sm_86 the plan-layer counts do not predict the kernel. Fewer intermediates -> less spill: MIXED (inversions: L7 b1 literal/no-sieve, L7 b1 literal/tuned, L7 b1 no-sieve/tuned, L10 b1 literal/no-sieve, L10 b1 literal/tuned, L10 b1 no-sieve/tuned, L10 b3 literal/no-sieve, L10 b3 literal/tuned, L10 b3 no-sieve/tuned, L13 b1 literal/tuned, L13 b1 no-sieve/tuned, L13 b6 literal/no-sieve, L13 b6 no-sieve/tuned, L16 b1 literal/tuned, L16 b6 literal/no-sieve, L16 b9 literal/no-sieve, L16 b9 no-sieve/tuned). Fewer FLOPs -> faster: wide-T MIXED (inversions: L16 b6 literal/no-sieve, L16 b12 literal/no-sieve); near-T MIXED (inversions: L16 b6 literal/no-sieve).
